title: Usage Pattern Change Detector with Contextual Alerting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a low-noise, context-aware detector that finds meaningful shifts in usage/cost/latency across customer routes and surfaces actionable alerts in the Console and alerting integrations. This ticket covers the backend detection service and the pipeline glue needed to compute per-customer and per-route baselines, attribute anomalies to features (batching, model, region), and push enriched alerts to the existing Alert Router.

Motivation: Current threshold-based alerts either miss slow drifts or generate noise for seasonal workloads. We need a detector that handles multiple timescales, adapts to changing baselines, and ties anomalies to context (deploys, rate-limit changes, billing plan events) to reduce false positives and enable faster triage.

Scope:
- Streaming detector service that subscribes to metrics topic (kafka://metrics-ingest) and writes anomaly events to alerts topic (kafka://console-alerts).
- Compute rolling multi-window baselines (1h, 24h, 7d) and a seasonal component for daily/hourly patterns.
- Use robust statistics (median absolute deviation + EWMA) plus event-aware suppression windows.
- Attribution metadata: top contributing routes, model, region, and whether a rollout/canary is in flight.
- Integrate with Alert Router for kill-switch, dedupe, and downstream delivery (Slack, Email, PagerDuty).

Non-goals: Model training pipelines, UI work (Console UX ticket will consume alerts), long-term historical reprocessing (separate infra task).
acceptance_criteria: Detector consumes metrics from metrics-ingest and emits anomaly events to console-alerts with required enrichment fields
Baseline computation supports 1h/24h/7d windows and declines false positives on known seasonal patterns in testing dataset
Alerts include attribution (route, model, region) and confidence score
Alerts can be suppressed by event tags (deploy, billing-change) and honor dedupe windows configured in Alert Router
Automated smoke tests validate detection behavior on replayed production traces and run in CI (pass threshold: >90% reduction in FP vs baseline thresholds)
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike detection prototype implemented in python (streaming worker) using kafka-python. Early results show reduced false positives for hourly seasonality but noisy during plan change events.

2026-02-25: Switched baseline from simple moving average to EWMA + MAD for robust outlier handling. Added 24h and 7d windows. Performance: worker handles 12k msg/s on a t3.xlarge equivalent in local perf tests.
2026-03-02: Added event ingestion for deploys and billing-change tags using sidecar subscription to event-store topic; initial suppression logic implemented (30m after deploy).
2026-03-07: Integration spike with Alert Router and dedupe keys completed. Started end-to-end tests replaying last 90 days; recall meets target but precision needs tuning on low-volume tenants.
2026-03-10: PR opened for Rust implementation of hot path (ENG-25701-rust-detector) to reduce tail latency. Seeking review from infra and SRE.
implementation_notes: Language: core detection implemented in Rust (memory & CPU efficient) with a Python shim for rapid experimentation.
State stores: Local RocksDB for per-partition baselines + periodic checkpointing to S3 for recovery.
Metric inputs: tokenized per-route counters, latency p95/p99 histograms, cost-per-token estimates emitted by billing pipeline.
Backfill: For initial rollout we will seed baselines from 30 days of historical aggregates run offline and then switch to streaming updates.
Observability: expose detector metrics (processing lag, anomalies/sec, false_positive_rate_est) to the Console and create dedicated dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High FP on low-volume tenants. Mitigation: add min-volume floor and fall back to aggregated-account-level baselines.
Risk: Detector state explosion across millions of routes. Mitigation: LRU eviction + compacted checkpoints + sample-based baselines for long-tail routes.
Risk: Correlated billing events causing mass alerts. Mitigation: global suppression window and root-cause tag propagation from billing service.
Risk: Increased pipeline load. Mitigation: use async batched writes and rate-limit detector consumption; run canaries in dedicated cluster.
review_feedback: PM review (Ravi Kumar): ensure clear SLAs for alert delivery; asked for prioritization of top-30 customers in rollout.
SRE review (Dana Lee): prefer Rust for steady-state worker; recommended RocksDB tuning and compaction windows.
Design review (Priya Menon): suggested adding an 'explain' payload that surfaces top-3 contributing dimensions for each alert.
qa_plan: Unit tests for baseline math and suppression logic
Synthetic workloads: replay of labeled incidents (spikes/drifts) with expected detection labels
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic and manual verification by SRE/Oncall
Post-launch tuning window (2 weeks) with guardrails to throttle noisy alerts
